optional_codes.reason: Furosemide, lisinopril and amlodipine are prescribed drugs taken every day for chronic conditions, which fits category Z79, but no Tabular List instruction requires the code. Defensible either way.

citations.I11.0: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.A.15: the word 'with' in the Alphabetic Index means 'associated with' or 'due to'; the classification presumes a causal relationship between two conditions linked by it, and they are coded as related even in the absence of provider documentation explicitly linking them, unless the documentation clearly states that they are unrelated. Section I.C.9.a: the classification presumes a causal relationship between hypertension and heart involvement. Section I.C.9.a.1: hypertension with a heart condition classified to I50.- is assigned to a code from category I11, with an additional code from category I50 to identify the heart condition. The Alphabetic Index lists 'heart failure' under 'Hypertension, with' at I11.0. Here the emergency physician lists acute on chronic diastolic heart failure and hypertension as two separate items, states no link and does not say that they are unrelated, so the two are reported with the code for hypertensive heart disease with heart failure. No chronic kidney disease is present.
citations.I50.33: Tabular List instruction at I11.0: use additional code to identify type of heart failure (I50.-); instruction at I50: code first heart failure due to hypertension (I11.0). Here the provider documents the heart failure as acute on chronic diastolic, so that code follows I11.0.

coder_notes: Counter-case: the combination code is the supported one. Reporting I10 beside I50.33 would treat the two conditions as unrelated, which only the provider's statement that they are unrelated would allow. The order is fixed by the Tabular List notes, although the heart failure is what brought her in. Shortness of breath, orthopnea and leg swelling are part of the heart failure and are not coded beside it (Section I.B.5). The pulmonary congestion on the chest X-ray and the raised natriuretic peptide are explained by the diagnosis; the oxygen saturation is a vital sign, and no hypoxemia is diagnosed. A blood pressure of 152/88 with no statement of urgency or emergency is not a hypertensive crisis. Chronic kidney disease, diabetes, coronary artery disease and atrial fibrillation are denied.
